title: Spiral galaxy NGC 4565
caption: The Needle Galaxy, NGC 4565, imaged by the Very Large Telescope
celestial: NGC 4565 · constellation Coma Berenices · about 30 million light-years away (source figure)

recognition.text: Official ESO press-release image. No published audience rating.

story: A spiral galaxy seen edge-on stretches across this image from ESO's Very Large Telescope, a bright yellowish bulge rising from its center above prominent lanes of dust. This is NGC 4565, known for obvious reasons as the Needle Galaxy.
Sir William Herschel, who also discovered Uranus, first spotted it in 1785. It is one of the most famous examples of an edge-on spiral and sits in Coma Berenices, some 30 million light-years from us.

Seeing a spiral from the side hides its arms but shows off its thin disc and the dust within it. NGC 4565 is relatively close, only 12 times farther than the Andromeda galaxy, and relatively large, roughly a third larger than the Milky Way. That combination means it does not quite fit inside the field of view of the FORS instrument used for this picture.
scale: Using the source's listed field of view (6.85 x 6.84 arcminutes) and distance (30 million light years), the frame spans roughly 60,000 × 60,000 light-years. Its light set out about 30 million years before reaching the telescope.

understand.summary: This image comes from the FORS instrument on the Very Large Telescope and combines B, V, R and I filters, spanning visible to near-infrared light. The color assigned to each filter is not published.
understand.eye: The galaxy is far too faint to see in this detail by eye. A large telescope collects far more light, and part of the data is near-infrared light the eye cannot detect.

behind.exposure: Not published on the source page.
behind.technique: Not stated by the source (single frame, stack, mosaic or panorama unknown).

explore: Many more distant galaxies are scattered across the background of this FORS image. They show why galaxies were once nicknamed island universes, meaning separate systems of stars floating in space. NGC 4565 itself spills past the frame.
alt: An edge-on spiral galaxy stretched like a needle across the frame, with a yellowish central bulge and dark dust lanes, and background galaxies around it.
